title: Measuring a school tower
body: During a mathematics activity, Riya stands at a point A on level ground, 30 m from the foot B of a vertical tower BC. Her teacher tells her that the straight line joining A to the top C of the tower makes an angle of 60° with the ground, so that triangle ABC is right-angled at B with angle BAC = 60°. Riya wants to find the height of the tower and the length of the line AC without climbing the tower, using only the trigonometric ratios of 60° (take the ground and the tower as straight lines).
